objects.description: Abstract base class that defines the interface for allocating and deleting raw character buffers. Provides two New overloads and a Delete function, plus an optional idle hint. Implementations must guarantee New never returns null and must pair allocations with Delete.

Functor/deleter type intended for use with std::unique_ptr<char[]> that were allocated by a QuicheBufferAllocator. Captures the allocator pointer and calls allocator->Delete on the buffer when invoked.

Type alias for a unique_ptr managing a char[] buffer with QuicheBufferDeleter. Owns buffers allocated via QuicheBufferAllocator. Note: this is an alias; pointer type here refers to the alias itself (QuicheUniqueBufferPtr) being used as a type name.

Owning, mutable buffer wrapper around a QuicheUniqueBufferPtr plus length. Provides construction from an allocator and size, from an existing unique buffer, move semantics, and factory helpers to copy from string_view or from iovec. Can be empty and can release ownership of the underlying buffer.
Concrete implementation of QuicheBufferAllocator that allocates and frees using new[]/delete[] on char arrays. Provides a singleton accessor via Get().

functions.name: quiche::QuicheBufferAllocator::New
functions.description: Allocates or returns a new buffer of exactly size bytes. Implementations must never return null. Used as the primary allocation entry point for buffer providers.
requirements: size is the number of bytes requested; zero-length behavior is unspecified by this interface
Return value must be non-null (as documented)
Caller is responsible for eventually releasing the buffer via quiche::QuicheBufferAllocator::Delete on the same allocator
The returned buffer must be compatible with delete semantics provided by this allocator

functions.name: quiche::QuicheBufferAllocator::New
functions.signature: virtual char* quiche::QuicheBufferAllocator::New(size_t size, bool flag_enable) = 0
functions.description: Allocates or returns a new buffer of size bytes, with behavior influenced by flag_enable. If flag_enable is true, behaves like New(size); otherwise returns a buffer compatible with allocations made directly with operator new. Must never return null.
requirements: size is the number of bytes requested; zero-length behavior is unspecified
Return value must be non-null (as documented)
Caller must release the returned buffer via this allocator’s Delete
Behavioral difference when flag_enable is false implies the returned buffer must be safe to manage with this allocator and compatible with operator new[] semantics

functions.name: quiche::QuicheBufferAllocator::Delete
functions.description: Releases a buffer previously obtained from this allocator.
requirements: buffer must have been allocated by the same quiche::QuicheBufferAllocator instance via one of its New overloads (inferred from typical allocator contracts)
Do not pass a buffer that has already been freed
Null handling is unspecified by this interface; callers should not assume Delete(nullptr) is safe unless documented by a concrete implementation

functions.name: quiche::QuicheBufferAllocator::MarkAllocatorIdle
functions.description: Advises the allocator that it is idle and may release held resources. This is a hint and may be a no-op.
requirements: May be called at any time; no ordering constraints are documented
Callers must not rely on any particular side effects; resource release is best-effort

functions.name: quiche::QuicheBufferDeleter::allocator
functions.description: Accesses the underlying allocator used by this deleter. Useful when managing buffers via std::unique_ptr with custom deleter.
requirements: The returned pointer may be null if the deleter was constructed with a null allocator (e.g., for empty buffers)
Callers must not use the returned allocator pointer after the allocator’s lifetime ends

functions.name: quiche::QuicheBufferDeleter::operator()
functions.description: Invokes allocator_->Delete(buffer) to free a buffer. Intended to be used as the custom deleter for QuicheUniqueBufferPtr.
requirements: allocator_ must be a valid, live quiche::QuicheBufferAllocator when invoked
buffer must be a buffer allocated by allocator_ via New
Behavior when buffer == nullptr depends on allocator_->Delete; callers should not rely on nullptr being acceptable unless guaranteed by the allocator

functions.name: quiche::MakeUniqueBuffer
functions.description: Allocates a new char[] buffer of size bytes from allocator and returns it wrapped in a unique_ptr with a QuicheBufferDeleter bound to allocator.
requirements: allocator must be non-null and must outlive the returned unique_ptr’s deleter invocation
size is the number of bytes requested; may be zero but resulting pointer/nullness follows allocator->New contract (never null per interface)
Caller should keep the allocator alive until the unique_ptr (and its copies/moves) is destroyed or reset

functions.name: quiche::QuicheBuffer::QuicheBuffer
functions.description: Default-constructs an empty QuicheBuffer. Holds no memory and has size 0.
requirements: No requirements; resulting buffer is empty and data() may return nullptr

functions.name: quiche::QuicheBuffer::QuicheBuffer
functions.description: Constructs a QuicheBuffer by allocating size bytes from allocator. The buffer is mutable and may be empty if size is 0.
requirements: allocator must be non-null and valid during construction
size is the number of bytes to allocate; zero creates an empty buffer
The allocator must fulfill the New contract (must not return null)

functions.name: quiche::QuicheBuffer::QuicheBuffer
functions.description: Constructs a QuicheBuffer that takes ownership of an existing unique buffer and associates a logical size with it.
requirements: buffer must have a valid deleter (QuicheBufferDeleter) that can free the memory it owns
size should match the actual allocated length of the buffer to avoid overreads/writes; not enforced by the constructor
After construction, the QuicheBuffer owns the buffer; the passed unique_ptr must not be used by the caller anymore

functions.name: quiche::QuicheBuffer::operator=
functions.description: Move-assigns from another QuicheBuffer, transferring ownership of the underlying buffer and size. The source is left empty.
requirements: other is an rvalue; after assignment, other should not be used to access prior data as it is set to empty by the implementation
Self-move-assignment behavior follows standard move semantics; no special requirements

functions.name: quiche::QuicheBuffer::Copy
functions.description: Creates a new QuicheBuffer that holds a copy of data. Allocates data.size() bytes and memcpy’s the contents.
requirements: allocator must be non-null and valid for allocation
data must reference readable memory of length data.size()
Resulting buffer size equals data.size(); may be 0 for empty data

functions.name: quiche::QuicheBuffer::CopyFromIovec
functions.signature: static quiche::QuicheBuffer quiche::QuicheBuffer::CopyFromIovec(quiche::QuicheBufferAllocator* allocator, const struct iovec* iov, int iov_count, size_t iov_offset, size_t buffer_length)
functions.description: Creates a new QuicheBuffer of length buffer_length and fills it by copying from a scatter/gather array of iovec starting at byte offset iov_offset. The total length available across iov must be at least iov_offset + buffer_length.
requirements: allocator must be non-null and valid
iov must be a non-null pointer to an array of at least iov_count iovec elements
iov_count must describe the number of elements in iov; it must be large enough that the total bytes across the array is at least iov_offset + buffer_length (as documented)
iov must contain at least iov_offset + buffer_length bytes in total (explicitly documented)
buffer_length is the number of bytes to copy; may be 0 to produce an empty buffer

functions.name: quiche::QuicheBuffer::data
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the underlying buffer data. Pointer may be null if the buffer is empty.
requirements: The returned pointer remains valid until the QuicheBuffer is destroyed, released, or moved-from
Do not dereference if size() == 0 or if the pointer is null

functions.name: quiche::QuicheBuffer::data
functions.description: Returns a mutable pointer to the underlying buffer data. Pointer may be null if the buffer is empty.
requirements: The returned pointer remains valid until the QuicheBuffer is destroyed, released, or moved-from
Do not dereference if size() == 0 or if the pointer is null
Mutating through the pointer must not exceed size() bytes

functions.name: quiche::QuicheBuffer::size
functions.description: Returns the current logical size in bytes of the buffer.
requirements: None

functions.name: quiche::QuicheBuffer::empty
functions.description: Returns true if size() == 0.
requirements: None

functions.name: quiche::QuicheBuffer::AsStringView
functions.description: Returns an absl::string_view over the buffer’s contents [data(), size()]. The view does not take ownership.
requirements: The returned view is only valid while the QuicheBuffer remains alive and unmodified in ways that reallocate or release the buffer
Do not use the view after calling Release() or after moving from the buffer

functions.name: quiche::QuicheBuffer::AsSpan
functions.description: Returns a mutable absl::Span<char> covering the entire buffer [data(), size()].
requirements: The returned span is only valid while the QuicheBuffer remains alive and the underlying storage is not released or moved
Do not use the span after calling Release() or moving

functions.name: quiche::QuicheBuffer::Release
functions.description: Releases ownership of the underlying unique buffer and returns it, setting this QuicheBuffer’s size to 0 and leaving it empty.
requirements: After Release(), this object no longer owns memory; data() will be nullptr and size() becomes 0
Caller becomes responsible for eventually freeing the returned unique_ptr (or letting it go out of scope)
Do not use any previously obtained views/spans after release

functions.name: quiche::SimpleBufferAllocator::Get
functions.description: Returns a pointer to a process-wide singleton SimpleBufferAllocator that allocates with operator new[]/delete[] on char arrays.
requirements: The returned pointer is a singleton; callers must not delete it
Thread-safety of the singleton initialization is provided by function-local static initialization; subsequent usage thread-safety is not documented

functions.name: quiche::SimpleBufferAllocator::New
functions.description: Allocates a new char[] buffer of size bytes using operator new[]. Never returns null per the base-class contract.
requirements: size is the number of bytes requested; operator new[] may throw on allocation failure in exception-enabled builds, otherwise the process may terminate
The returned buffer must be freed with quiche::SimpleBufferAllocator::Delete (or via the matching QuicheBufferDeleter)

functions.name: quiche::SimpleBufferAllocator::New
functions.signature: char* quiche::SimpleBufferAllocator::New(size_t size, bool flag_enable) override
functions.description: Allocates a new char[] buffer of size bytes. The flag may be used by the implementation but callers should not depend on its behavior. Must not return null per base-class contract.
requirements: size is the number of bytes requested
Caller must free the buffer via quiche::SimpleBufferAllocator::Delete (or via its deleter)
Behavioral differences based on flag_enable are not specified and should not be relied upon

functions.name: quiche::SimpleBufferAllocator::Delete
functions.description: Frees a char[] buffer previously allocated by this allocator, typically via operator delete[].
requirements: buffer must have been allocated by quiche::SimpleBufferAllocator::New from this allocator
Do not pass memory not obtained from this allocator
Passing nullptr is unspecified by interface; do not assume it is allowed

data_types.description: A byte buffer with no required encoding or structure. May contain any 8-bit values including null bytes. Suitable for functions that copy or process raw memory or generic string_view data without format constraints.
